title: Reap: Uncovering Monte Carlo proof search with a lightweight model
summary: The authors report that later RL checkpoints make fewer explicit search decisions while completing more work per tactic action and organizing proofs around intermediate claims; Reaper-1 reaches 79.9% pass@32 on miniF2F-test. All successful proofs are replayed and checked by Lean’s kernel; evaluation covers miniF2F, ProofNet, FATE-M, PutnamBench, and CombiBench with benchmark decontamination. The paper frames the proof-search behavior claim as a pattern supported by quantitative traces and case studies.
ai_technology: Reaper-1 uses policy/value-guided MCTS in Lean; structured action logs analyze proof search as the model learns from continued pretraining, supervised tactic learning, and iterative reinforcement learning.
